To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the soft-gluon contributions to the q_T and y distributions at the LHC are large, and that soft-gluon corrections are essential to describe the data in a reliable way, especially at low q_T and y.

the soft-gluon corrections are large and negative in the small q_T region, and that the resummation of these soft corrections to all orders improves significantly the agreement of theoretical predictions with the experimental data.

the NNLL corrections are very large and negative in the small-qT region (qT < 20 GeV), while in the large-qT region (20 GeV < qT < 100 GeV) the NNLL corrections have a moderate positive impact on the NLO predictions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Higgs differential distributions in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (pQCD).
a detailed study of the Higgs production cross section at the LHC, with a focus on the transverse-momenta and rapidities of the Higgs particle.
the study of the transverse-momenta (q_T) distribution of the Higgs at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theoretical uncertainties on the total cross section are under control at the NLO + NNLL accuracy.
the soft-gluon-resummed predictions for the q_T and y distributions at the NNLL order are in excellent agreement with the fixed-order NLO results for q_T ~ M_H and for all y values.
the theoretical uncertainty in the Higgs cross section is now well under control and that the LHC is ready for the discovery and study of a light Higgs boson.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the Higgs bosons with transverse momenta up to 200 GeV, the NNLL resummation reduces the theoretical uncertainties by more than a factor two with respect to the NLO calculation.

we have computed the NNLO corrections to the Higgs production cross section at the LHC, and the resummation at NNLL of the logarithmically-enhanced terms in the Higgs transverse-momentum and rapidity distributions at the LHC.
the resummed cross section is in good agreement with the fixed order NLO result for all values of q_T and y.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, at least at the 14 TeV LHC, soft-gluon corrections are not very important for the q_T distribution of the Higgs, while they are very important in the y distribution.
, in order to have a reliable theoretical prediction for the Higgs transverse-momentum distribution, it is mandatory to include soft-gluon contributions beyond NLO.
the resummation effect in the small-q region is significant for the Higgs bosons produced at the LHC.
